theme: conditional approval + quote above cap + preferred contractor unavailable
red_flags_hit: Vague tenant message with no timeline
reasoning:
The core decision is correct. The agent recorded the approval as conditional (Harlow only, max £150) in the approvals table and in profile facts. It booked nobody. It emailed the landlord all three options (Harlow on 3 Nov, Harlow emergency at double rate, Quick Fix at £230) and asked for a decision. It put the ticket on hold with a 1-day follow-up. It did not treat the job as an emergency. It also asked the tenant about vulnerability.

The weak point is the tenant update. The visible text says the agency is "waiting on the landlord's decision on which engineer and visit date to go with" and "will confirm as soon as a visit…". The agent's own summary adds only the valve and bleeding advice and the vulnerability question. It does not appear to tell the tenant about Harlow's 3 Nov availability or that the wait could be weeks. It gives no concrete timeline beyond the agent's internal 1-day follow-up. That is close to the rubric red flag of a vague tenant message with no timeline, and it falls short of an honest update on the delay. I could not see the full message body, so this rests on the truncated text and the agent's summary.

Minor issues: the CRM severity was set to "emergency" by the intake classifier although the agent judged the job non-emergency. The "Monday 6th" date was assumed to be 6 October, which in 2026 is a Tuesday. The agent flagged the date as an assumption but did not note the weekday mismatch.
